Copy.m483: Barry Halliwell reviews how antioxidants act in the body and where the evidence is weaker than the marketing. Free radicals also do useful jobs, and more antioxidant is not automatically better.
Copy.m485: A review of how physical activity builds and maintains healthy mitochondria in muscle. Movement remains the best-supported way to care for them.
Copy.m487: Mattson and Arumugam describe the hallmarks of brain aging, including changes in energy metabolism and mitochondria. A map of the biology, not a treatment guide.
Copy.m489: Picard and McEwen propose a framework for how psychological stress affects mitochondria, drawn mostly from animal and cell studies. An idea being tested, not a settled fact.
Copy.m491: Sun, Youle and Finkel review the evidence that mitochondrial decline is part of how cells age, and the open questions. Mechanisms, not a product claim.
Copy.m493: Magistretti and Allaman explain how brain cells produce and share energy. Background on why mental energy is, at bottom, a cellular question.
Copy.m495: A review of 78 trials found no evidence that antioxidant supplements help people live longer, and a possible harm from beta-carotene and vitamin E at high doses. Balance for the whole topic.
Copy.m496: Where the free-radical idea came from
Copy.m497: Denham Harman's original proposal that free radicals drive aging. Parts of the theory have since been revised, but it started the field.
Copy.m498: A companion study of the same two nutrients
Copy.m499: Hagen and colleagues, in a companion paper to the Liu study, tested acetyl-L-carnitine and lipoic acid in aging animals and measured metabolic function and oxidative stress. An animal study, not a human trial.
Copy.m500: Dr. Liu on lipoic acid and the aging brain
Copy.m501: An overview by Dr. Jiankang Liu of how alpha-lipoic acid may support aging mitochondria and memory in animal studies. Written by our scientist; mostly animal work.
Copy.m502: Creatine and thinking in healthy adults
Copy.m503: A systematic review of six small trials found creatine may help short-term memory and reasoning in healthy people, with mixed results elsewhere. Small studies; more work needed.
Copy.m505: Shay and colleagues review what lipoic acid does in the body and what supplement studies suggest. Mechanisms are clearer than human benefits.
Copy.m507: A meta-analysis of trials in people with mild cognitive impairment or mild Alzheimer's disease reported a benefit over placebo. Patients, not healthy adults; older trials.
Copy.m509: A Cochrane review found no clear evidence of benefit in dementia. Shown beside the pooled trials above so both readings are visible.
Copy.m510: Longvida curcumin in healthy older adults
Copy.m511: Cox and colleagues gave 60 healthy adults aged 60 to 85 the Longvida curcumin preparation for four weeks and reported changes in attention, working memory and mood. The same preparation Turmerific uses; a small, short study.
Copy.m513: Small and colleagues followed 40 adults without dementia for 18 months on a different curcumin preparation, Theracurmin, and reported memory changes. Another preparation, a small group.
Copy.m515: Nelson and colleagues explain why curcumin is poorly absorbed and why many laboratory results have not held up. A skeptical review, included on purpose.
Copy.m516: Grape seed extract and blood pressure
Copy.m517: A meta-analysis of nine trials found a modest drop in systolic blood pressure and heart rate with grape seed extract, and no change in cholesterol. Modest effects in short trials.
Copy.m518: Pine bark extract: a trial that found nothing
Copy.m519: A 12-week trial of pine bark extract in 130 adults found no effect on blood pressure, cholesterol or other heart-risk markers. A null result, shown because honesty matters.
Copy.m520: Artepillin C, the key compound in green propolis
Copy.m521: A review of the chemistry, absorption and laboratory findings for artepillin C, the compound Brazilian green propolis is known for. Mostly laboratory studies; few human trials.
Copy.m522: What has been tested about propolis
Copy.m523: A review of experimental studies on propolis from different regions. Composition varies with the plants bees visit, so results do not transfer between products.
Copy.m525: A review of coenzyme Q10's role in cellular energy and what supplement trials in aging and disease have shown. Mixed trial results.
Copy.m527: Thirty healthy adults took L-theanine for four weeks and reported fewer stress-related symptoms than on placebo. Small and short; healthy volunteers.
Copy.m529: Seventy-eight older Japanese adults with memory complaints took soybean phosphatidylserine for six months; those with lower scores at the start improved more. One trial, one group.

Copy.m533: The National Institute on Aging on what helps keep thinking skills as we age, and which claims are not backed by evidence.
